title: Business case for AI retention experimentation platform
summary: Build a business case for AI retention platform using churn revenue, measurable retention lift, expected payback, and the cost of implementation.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR**


A business case for AI retention experimentation software should demonstrate three things.


- How much subscription revenue is exposed to churn
- What additional revenue a measurable improvement in retention could generate
- What it will cost to achieve that improvement


‍


Subscription businesses already invest in churn prediction, CRM automation, and customer analytics. When evaluating AI retention experimentation software, the challenge is establishing what additional value the investment can deliver and whether that value justifies its cost.


The business case needs to connect retention experiments with financial outcomes. This means identifying the subscriber audiences worth targeting, measuring how many additional subscribers are retained compared with a control group, and calculating the resulting revenue against the cost of the software. These figures give finance a basis for assessing the investment and its expected payback.


## Calculating revenue at risk from churn


Start with your active subscriber count, monthly churn rate, and average revenue per user (ARPU).


> Annualized churn revenue exposure = Active subscribers × Monthly churn rate × Monthly ARPU × 12


For example, a publisher with 100,000 subscribers, a 4% monthly churn rate, and $20 monthly ARPU loses approximately 4,000 subscribers and $80,000 in recurring revenue each month. At that pace, annualized churn revenue exposure is $960,000. This represents the annualized rate of recurring revenue loss, rather than a forecast of actual revenue lost over the next 12 months.


### Identifying where churn is concentrated


A company-wide churn rate can hide significant differences between subscriber audiences. New subscribers with declining engagement, customers approaching a price increase, and previously active subscribers becoming dormant may have different cancellation risks.


Review[cohort retention rates](https://www.subsets.com/glossary/metrics/cohort-retention-rate) by subscription tenure, pricing, acquisition source, and product usage to identify the audiences with the greatest revenue exposure.


The business case should focus on audiences where retention experiments have the potential to generate a measurable commercial return.


## Estimating the revenue from improving retention


Calculate the potential revenue from additional subscribers retained within a defined audience.


> Incremental retained subscribers = Eligible audience × Retention lift expressed as a decimal


> Incremental revenue = Additional retained subscribers × Monthly ARPU × Additional months retained


Suppose a subscription business identifies 50,000 subscribers eligible for a retention experiment, with monthly ARPU of $20. A two-percentage-point retention lift would retain 1,000 additional subscribers compared with the control group. If those subscribers remain for six additional months, the estimated incremental subscription revenue is $120,000. The expected additional subscription duration should come from historical retention data.


## Three financial scenarios


Finance should receive conservative, base, and optimistic projections. Using the same audience of 50,000 subscribers, $20 monthly ARPU, and six additional retained months:


- **Low case** : A 0.5-percentage-point lift generates $30,000 in incremental revenue.
- **Base case** : A 1.5-percentage-point lift generates $90,000.
- **High case** : A three-percentage-point lift generates $180,000.


*These figures are illustrative. The actual business case should use your subscriber data and account for the costs of delivering each lifecycle flow.*


## Supporting the investment with retention results


Published customer results can help establish the potential value of retention experimentation, although financial projections should remain grounded in your own subscriber data.


- **Hearst** used Subsets to target subscribers showing churn-related behaviors before an introductory price increase. The experiments achieved a[3.4-percentage-point retention lift at Times Union and 2.3 percentage points at Houston Chronicle](https://www.subsets.com/customer-stories/hearst-increase-in-retention-using-lookalike-churn-audiences) .
- **DailyMail+** tested personalized content recommendations across five behavioral audiences. Three achieved statistically significant[retention lifts of 6.2, 4.9, and 5.3 percentage points](https://www.subsets.com/customer-stories/dailymail-retention-boost-with-personalized-content-recommendations) .
- **Matas** achieved a[29-percentage-point retention lift within 30 days](https://www.subsets.com/customer-stories/how-matas-increased-retention-by-29-with-subsets) among dormant Club Matas Plus subscribers, alongside 20% more orders.
- **The Independent** tested a personalization flow across two audiences. One achieved a[3.9-percentage-point retention lift](https://www.subsets.com/customer-stories/the-independent-personalization-flow-results-for-multiple-audiences) , while another recorded an observed 6.1-percentage-point decline that was not statistically significant.


Controlled experiments help teams establish which lifecycle flows improve retention before expanding them to additional subscribers.


## Calculating total investment & expected payback


The cost of retention experimentation software includes the license, implementation, data integration, and internal resources needed to manage experiments.


If the business is considering an internal solution, compare the full development cost. A churn prediction model identifies subscribers at risk, but running experiments also requires audience management, control groups, statistical analysis, and automation.


### Calculate payback


> Estimated payback in months = Investment to recover ÷ Monthly incremental financial contribution


Using the earlier base scenario, $90,000 in incremental subscription revenue over six months equals $15,000 per month if the revenue arrives evenly. With a total investment of $65,000 and an assumed contribution margin of 80%, the monthly incremental contribution would be $12,000, resulting in an estimated payback period of 5.4 months after the additional revenue begins.


A final financial model should account for implementation timing, operating costs, and when the additional revenue will be collected.


## Defining how investment will be measured


Before purchasing software, establish a plan for testing its commercial impact.


Start with two or three subscriber audiences, each with a defined retention objective and its own control group. Agree on the minimum retention lift, statistical requirements, observation period, and date for reviewing results.


The ideal AI retention[experimentation platform](https://www.subsets.com/experiment) should be able to support controlled lifecycle testing and automated statistical analysis. Successful experiments can become[ongoing lifecycle flows](https://www.subsets.com/automate) , with control groups maintained to measure continued performance. The decision to expand or discontinue an experiment should depend on its measured retention impact and financial contribution.


## What to evaluate before choosing AI retention experimentation software


Compare vendors on the capabilities directly connected to measurable retention improvements.


1. **Behavioral audiences and experiment design:** The platform should identify relevant behavioral audiences, explain their churn-related characteristics, and support simultaneous experiments with treatment and control groups. Ask the vendor to demonstrate how audiences are selected and experiments are configured.
2. **Retention measurement:** The system should report incremental retention lift in percentage points, including statistical significance, and connect results to subscription revenue and lifetime value. Request a completed experiment showing its audience, control group, measurement period, and commercial outcome.
3. **Automation** : Successful experiments should become ongoing lifecycle flows while retaining control groups for continued measurement.Confirm how new subscribers enter automated flows and how performance is monitored.
4. **Integration and implementation:** The software should be able to[integrate](https://www.subsets.com/integrations) with existing subscription, data, and customer engagement systems. Ask the vendor for an implementation plan covering integration requirements, responsibilities, and the first experiment readout.
5. **Security and customer evidence:** Review data handling requirements, certifications, and privacy documentation. Prioritize vendors with published retention results from businesses operating similar subscription models.


## Presenting the business case


Summarize the annualized revenue exposed to churn, the audiences with the greatest retention opportunity, and the projected revenue from improving retention. Include the total software and implementation costs, expected payback, and low, base, and high financial scenarios. Define the experiments, minimum retention lift required for success, and review date so finance can evaluate the investment against measurable results.
